scenario: AITA for visiting my son unannounced. | My son’s(19) in an university. He’s in a different city and lives in an apartment with 2 of his friends. Ever since he left(2 months ago) he just started ignoring me. I didn’t call him excessively, maybe once in two days. He’d hang up or not answer and text me later that he’s busy. Few days ago I was in the city for unrelated reason. I called him because I wanted to visit him but he didn’t answer so I just went to the apartment. His friend answered the door, my son was sleeping. The apartment was filthy, empty bottles everywhere, 5 or more ashtrays filled with cigarette butts. Dirty dishes to the roof. I joked about the place needing a good clean and he just rolled his eyes. I asked him why he was ignoring me. He said that he’s just busy with studying and all that stuff and I should give him space when he needs it. He also said that it was weird that I just showed up unannounced.

This can lead to a sense of disempowerment, as if you're simply following a script rather than forging your own path. prediction.raw: I think the answer is 1 (YTA - You're The Asshole). As a parent, it's natural to want to stay connected with your child, especially when they're away at university. However, it's essential to respect their boundaries and independence. By showing up unannounced, you disregarded your son's clear signals that he needed space and time to focus on his studies. Your son had been ignoring your calls or not answering, and then texting you later to say he was busy. This suggests that he was trying to set boundaries and communicate his needs to you. Instead of respecting those boundaries, you chose to show up at his apartment without warning, which can be perceived as intrusive and overbearing. Additionally, your comments about the state of the apartment, although perhaps well-intentioned, came across as judgmental and critical. Your son's response, rolling his eyes and seeming annoyed, suggests that he felt embarrassed or defensive about his living situation. It's understandable that you want to stay connected with your son, but it's crucial to find a balance between showing interest and respect for his independence. In this case, it would have been better to respect his boundaries and wait for him to initiate contact or respond to your calls. By doing so, you can rebuild trust and strengthen your relationship with your son, rather than potentially damaging it by overstepping and being perceived as controlling.
